source.excerpt: Men give me credit for genius; but all the genius I have lies in this: when I have a subject on hand I study it profoundly.
trail: The July 1924 NOW scan, page 16, prints a shorter variant ending with labor and thought and credits Hamilton. Bard repeats a longer version. Neither supplies an eighteenth-century document. The 1924 scan was downloaded and its text independently read; it verifies circulation, not Hamilton’s authorship. The 1924 printed attribution ↗
Bard publishes a longer variant credited to Hamilton without a primary citation. Bard’s longer version ↗

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: A 1924 motivational magazine credits Hamilton with a shorter statement about study, labor and thought. That is evidence of twentieth-century circulation, but the inspected magazine does not supply a Hamilton-era letter or speech for the much longer popular passage.
